full_caption: Lucian Marchetti-Doyle, Appellant, v. Nikolai Grimsby-Hale, Appellee
court: Marrowdale District Court of Appeal, Fourth District
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Lucian Marchetti-Doyle claims title by adverse possession to a 5.2-acre wooded tract adjoining 4520 Old Quarry Turnpike, Lindenmere, MD, of which Nikolai Grimsby-Hale is the record owner.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: The trial court found the elements satisfied as to 40.2 acres and not satisfied as to the remainder, which lay beyond any fence or posted line. That allocation is not clearly erroneous.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: Payment of property taxes is not an independent element in this jurisdiction but is evidence bearing on the notoriety of the claim. Lucian Marchetti-Doyle paid taxes assessed against the tract for 7 of the 10 years in question.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: Color of title is not required where the claim rests on actual occupancy, but it enlarges the claim to the full extent of the described premises rather than the portion actually occupied.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: Land held by a municipality for a public purpose is not subject to adverse possession. The 25-foot strip within the platted right of way is therefore excluded from any judgment in Lucian Marchetti-Doyle's favor.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: Lucian Marchetti-Doyle posted the tract against trespass in 2002, cut and sold standing timber in 2012 and 2018, and maintained a hunting camp on the northeast quarter continuously thereafter.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: Possession is 'actual' where the claimant uses the land as an ordinary owner of similar land would use it. For wooded acreage, selective timbering, posting, and seasonal recreational use may suffice where cultivation would not be expected.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: Continuity is broken by an entry of the record owner made with intent to reclaim possession. The single survey visit by Nikolai Grimsby-Hale's agent in 2035, unaccompanied by any assertion of possession, did not interrupt the running of the statute.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: Affirmed in part, reversed in part, and remanded for entry of a decree describing the vested tract by metes and bounds consistent with the surveyor's Exhibit E-2.

sections.heading: RIDER 2 — ACTS OF POSSESSION RELIED UPON
sections.text: Claimant relies upon the following acts, each continuing from the date shown through the date of filing: posting of the perimeter against trespass beginning in 2002; commercial timber harvest in 2012 and 2018; construction and continuous seasonal use of a hunting camp; annual maintenance of the interior access track; and payment of the real property taxes assessed against the tract for 7 of the 10 years preceding this claim.

sections.heading: RIDER 3 — TACKING AND PRIVITY
sections.text: Claimant tacks to its own possession the 7 years of possession of its immediate predecessor in interest, with whom Claimant is in privity by virtue of the deed recorded at Book 4545, Page 46, which deed purported to convey the disputed tract and thereby transferred the possessory claim along with the record title.

sections.heading: RIDER 5 — QUIET TITLE RELIEF REQUESTED
sections.text: Claimant requests a decree quieting title in Claimant as against Respondent and all persons claiming under Respondent, describing the vested tract by metes and bounds, directing the Recorder to index the decree against both parcels, and awarding costs. Claimant does not seek damages for the period of possession.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Entire Agreement and Riders
sections.text: This instrument, together with the exhibits and riders attached and incorporated by reference, constitutes the entire agreement of the parties and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations and agreements, whether oral or written. In the event of a conflict between a printed provision and a rider, the rider shall control, the rider being the specifically negotiated expression of the parties' intent.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Notice
sections.text: Every notice required or permitted shall be in writing and shall be deemed given: on personal delivery; on the third business day after deposit in the United States mail, certified, return receipt requested, postage prepaid; or on the next business day after deposit with a nationally recognized overnight courier. Notices to a party shall be sent to the address last furnished by that party in writing. Electronic mail alone does not constitute notice unless the recipient acknowledges receipt in writing.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Waiver and Course of Dealing
sections.text: No waiver of any breach shall be effective unless in writing and signed by the party charged. The acceptance of a payment with knowledge of a breach, the failure to insist on strict performance, or any course of dealing between the parties shall not constitute a waiver of that or any subsequent breach, nor estop the party from enforcing the provision thereafter.

sections.heading: Clause 4 — Dispute Resolution
sections.text: Before filing suit, a party shall give written notice of the dispute and the parties shall confer in good faith for not fewer than 3 days, and shall thereafter submit the dispute to non-binding mediation before a mediator experienced in real property matters. This clause does not bar an action for injunctive relief to prevent irreparable harm or an action to preserve the status quo.
